items.title:
Thank you for the numbers.

Let's use them.

780 men detained.

Fewer than 30 ever charged.

That means roughly 96% of the men the United States held in Guantánamo Bay, some for years, some for over a decade, were released without ever being accused of a specific crime in any legal proceeding.

You've just made the original argument more precisely than I did.

A system that detains 780 people and charges 30 is not a justice system.

Call it what you want. Don't call it justice.

"Law-of-war detention reviewed by administrative boards" is a long phrase for a short reality: men held indefinitely without the rights your country grades other countries on providing.

The numbers you cited are the indictment.
